text: It doesn't live up to the "international" name because of one rotten apple (the service in some departments). I took my father for a scheduled check-up and wanted to use his insurance and vehicle registration. I didn't know where to inform them. While my father was signing in front of the emergency room in Building 2, I asked a plump woman in a sweet, polite voice, "If we want to use insurance and the vehicle registration, where do we need to inform them?" (Because I didn't know, I asked out of ignorance). She replied, "What kind of insurance?" (I started gritting my teeth, thinking she probably didn't hear or understand what I asked). So I asked again (still in my usual polite tone), "The insurance that we'll use for the check-up appointment." And she answered, "This is it!" and pointed to the documents my father was signing. That was a terrible answer. I became annoyed and went back to wait for the check-up, which took a very long time, over an hour. When they called my father (the examination itself probably lasted less than a minute; he had a car accident and broke his collarbone), that wasn't too bad. After the examination, no one told my father where to go. I told him they probably wanted him to wait until they called him and then follow instructions. But he sat and waited for a very long time, seeing other people finish their examinations and leave. So I decided to go ask the same woman again, still using the same polite tone as before, "Excuse me, where do I need to go next?" She immediately retorted, "Ask the nurse!!" (That was awful!) So I went to ask a nurse who was nearby, explaining where I needed to go next. I said that since I'd finished my checkup, no one had told me what to do next. The nurse quickly checked and told me I could go to the pharmacy building. I must say, the nurses and staff in other departments were very polite and helpful. But as for this woman, I'm boycotting her; I'll make sure to be firm with her next time I see her. And while she was working, she was chatting loudly over a patient's head while they were filling out forms. I'd like to suggest that the hospital should call her in for etiquette training and screen their staff more carefully.
